question: Does prior strong-chorus history of the same species at a physical SiteID predict wet-survey strong chorus beyond the site's generic history of supporting strong choruses by other species?
population: Physically stable matched pairs with at least one prior eligible run in the same State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum. Focal species are route-new in the wet survey and were recorded somewhere on the route before the focal pair.
unit: pair x focal species x physical stop

predictors.same_species_prior_strong: 1 if the focal species had CallingIndex 2-3 at the SiteID in any eligible run strictly before the earlier focal-pair year.
predictors.other_species_prior_strong_richness: Number of other species that had CallingIndex 2-3 at that SiteID in prior eligible runs.
predictors.prior_site_effort: Number of prior eligible runs in which that SiteID was sampled; included to prevent richer site history from masquerading as site quality.

primary_design: Within each pair x species, demean wet_strong, same_species_prior_strong, log1p(other_species_prior_strong_richness), and prior_site_effort. Fit OLS without intercept with route-clustered covariance.
primary_prediction: Coefficient on same_species_prior_strong >0 with complete 95% CI >0 after simultaneous adjustment for generic other-species chorus history and prior site effort.
secondary: Report coefficient for other-species chorus richness as a generic-site-quality signal.
Report same-species rain_contrast interaction after pair-species demeaning as descriptive only.
minimum_gate: At least 500 informative pair x species groups with within-group variation in same_species_prior_strong, >=250 routes, and >=20 species.
interpretation: Support means local acoustic recurrence is species-specific beyond a generic propensity of the SiteID to support choruses.
It remains compatible with species-specific habitat matching or persistent local populations; it does not prove biological memory, continuous occupancy, or individual site fidelity.
No causal rainfall or reproductive-success claim.
